item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 211742
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Mon Sep 21 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
A tropical wave is forecast to move off western Africa by
Wednesday. Development, if any, of this system should be slow to
occur while it moves near the Cabo Verde Islands later this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Fay (AT1/AL062026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FAY GRADUALLY WEAKENING... As of 9:00 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 the center of Fay was located near 33.1, -32.2 with movement SSW at 3 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1004 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 212034
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026
 
...FAY GRADUALLY WEAKENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.1N 32.2W
ABOUT 445 MI...720 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SSW OR 210 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 33.1 North, longitude 32.2 West.  Fay is 
moving toward the south-southwest near 3 mph (6 km/h) and a gradual 
turn toward the southwest and west is expected during the next few 
days
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued weakening is forecast, and Fay is 
likely to degenerate into a post-tropical remnant low by late 
Tuesday.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 212036
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026

Strong west-northwesterly vertical wind shear has been affecting 
Fay today, with most or all deep convection being displaced well 
east of the well-defined low-level center.  Scatterometer data 
suggest that the peak winds have diminished to near 40 kt, which 
will be the advisory intensity estimate.

Global model forecasts show that a strong upper-level trough will 
shift eastward away from Fay during the next day or so.  This will 
likely lessen the wind shear over the system by late tomorrow.  
However, the Decay-SHIPS guidance indicates that the cyclone should 
be ingesting drier air during the next few days.  This is consistent 
with simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF global model, which 
shows the system losing most of its associated deep convection 
during the next 48 hours or so.  Therefore the NHC forecast shows 
Fay becoming a post-tropical remnant low by tomorrow night, and this 
event could occur even sooner than that.

Fay is moving slowly south-southwestward along the eastern side of 
a mid-level high.  The cyclone is expected to turn southwestward 
and then westward around the southern portion of the high until 
dissipation.  The official track forecast is similar to the 
previous few NHC forecasts.  This is also in good agreement with 
the latest GFS prediction.
